question: A line joining two end points is called a/an:
solution:
Note down some definitions:

 
• Parallel Line: Parallel lines don’t cross each other. In the language of linear equations, this means that they have the same slope. Parallel lines are lines that are on the same plane in three dimensions and do not intersect.
 
• Line-segment (definition): The set of two distinct points A, B and the points between them is known as the line-segment determined by A and B.
 
• **Intersecting line**: When two lines cross each other at a common point, we call them intersecting lines. This common point is known as the point of intersection. 

Hence, the above statement is of line segment length.
